description: USGS's magnitude 4.5+ earthquakes of the past week, read from GeoJSON with Polars, ranked, and plotted on a world projection (hover a quake for its place, depth and time; click for its USGS event page). Statistics: the Gutenberg–Richter law, a power law: the number of quakes at least as strong as M falls about tenfold per magnitude, so on a log axis it is a straight line whose slope is the b-value (Aki's maximum-likelihood estimate, with its standard error). A week has only about a hundred M4.5+ quakes, so b is uncertain to about ±0.1; the catalogue mixes magnitude types (mb, Mww) and is complete only above about M4.5.
name: Earthquakes this week
